title: Object Storage: outage concession and cash return
content:
Object Storage A customer seeks return of excess cash on an untaxed storage invoice with a completed provider incident and one completed original payment. The terminal state contains the adjudicated service concession and the customer-authorized original-destination refund.

## Ordered business actions

1. The customer themselves performs the customer claim amount action using file_storage_outage_claim_6a92fd5d.
2. The agent performs the accountant approved concession action using assess_storage_outage_30bc4acc.
3. The agent performs the signed concession credit action using post_storage_service_concession_cfd2170f.
4. The customer themselves performs the customer exact refund authorization action using authorize_storage_refund_9b3e6afe.
5. The agent performs the cash refund action using refund_storage_overpayment_1b2c5ab5.

## Object continuity

The filed claim reference is the assessment request reference. The approved assessment reference becomes the concession supporting evidence reference. The posted concession reference becomes the authorization supporting evidence reference. The exact authorization request reference becomes the payout authorization reference.

## Ordering basis

The customer claim is the basis of the accountant assessment; an unfiled claim supplies no claimed amount. The approved assessment is the basis of the financial concession; an unapproved result supplies no money authority. The concession must be posted before its resulting cash balance can be authorized. The exact customer authorization must exist before its cash payout. Each action is a synchronous filing, accountant calculation or financial booking against a completed report or payment; no physical or external event is manufactured.

## Hypothetical swapped actions

If the financial concession were placed before the approved assessment, that financial action would lack the assessment that supplies money authority. If payout preceded the exact authorization, it would lack customer authorization.
